Let $X\_1, X\_2, X\_3$ are three independent and identically distributed random variables with mean $\\mu$ and variance $\\sigma^2.$ Given below are $3$ different formulations of sample mean. (Observe that $E\[A\] = E\[B\]=E\[C\]).$  
$\\begin{aligned} A=& \\frac{X\_1+X\_2+X\_3}{3}\\\\ B=& {0.1X\_1+0.3X\_2+0.6X\_3}\\\\ C=& {0.2X\_1+0.3X\_2+0.5X\_3} \\end{aligned}$  
  
Choose the correct option from the following:

$\\text{Var}(A)= \\text{Var}(B)=\\text{Var}(C)$

$\\text{Var}(A)\\geq \\text{Var}(B)\\geq \\text{Var}(C)$

$\\text{Var}(A)\\leq \\text{Var}(B)\\leq \\text{Var}(C)$

$\\text{Var}(A)\\leq \\text{Var}(C)\\leq \\text{Var}(B)$

### Yes, the answer is correct.  
Score: 1

### Accepted Answers:

$\\text{Var}(A)\\leq \\text{Var}(C)\\leq \\text{Var}(B)$
